title: Open Problem (exact exponent for maximal cliques in c-closed graphs)
statement_text: For a fixed positive integer $c$, determine the exact exponent of $n$ (between $3/2$ and $2 - 2^{1-c}$) in the expression for the maximum number of maximal cliques in a $c$-closed graph on $n$ vertices.
context_text: For a positive integer $c$, a graph is $c$-closed if any two distinct vertices with at least $c$ common neighbours are adjacent. This models triadic closure in social networks: $1$-closed graphs are disjoint unions of cliques, $c=n-1$ allows all graphs, and $2$-closed graphs are exactly the graphs with no induced $C_4$ or diamond ($K_4$ minus an edge), e.g. graphs of girth at least $5$. A maximal clique is a clique not contained in a larger one. The authors prove that every $c$-closed $n$-vertex graph has at most $\min\{3^{(c-1)/3}n^2,\,4^{(c+4)(c-1)/2}n^{2-2^{1-c}}\}$ maximal cliques, so for constant $c$ the number is $O(n^{2-2^{1-c}})$ (e.g. $O(n^{3/2})$, $O(n^{7/4})$, $O(n^{15/8})$ for $c=2,3,4$), and conversely construct, for every $c$, $c$-closed graphs with $\Omega(c^{-3/2}2^{c/2}n^{3/2})$ maximal cliques (from girth-$5$ graphs). For $c=2$ the answer $\Theta(n^{3/2})$ was known (Eschen, Hoàng, Spinrad and Sritharan, via projective planes), so the question concerns $c\ge3$. The authors also show that $c$-closed $K_k$-free graphs attaining the upper bound would need a specific distribution of clique sizes: such graphs have $O(n^{3/2})$ edges and $n_{j+1}(G)=O(n_j(G)^{1/2}n)$, where $n_j(G)$ is the number of $K_j$'s.
